news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement after 23 years with Portugal
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo has officially announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to an extraordinary 23-year career with Portugal. The 41-year-old football legend confirmed the decision on Thursday, November 5, 2026, in an emotional video shared on social media. The announcement marks the end of an era for Portuguese football, with Ronaldo stepping away from the national team after becoming the most-capped player and highest goalscorer in men's international football history. However, Cristiano Ronaldo is not retiring from professional football entirely.

news.title: Europe's top international scorers: Cristiano Ronaldo out in front, ahead of Romelu Lukaku, Robert Lewandowski and Harry Kane
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo scored a staggering 146 international goals for Portugal. Who else is among the leading goalscorers? Cristiano Ronaldo retires from duty for Portugal having become the first European to reach 100 international goals in autumn 2020 – and remains well out in front as both Europe's and the world's all-time leading scorer. He marked his 200th Portugal appearance with an 89th-minute winner in Iceland on 20 June 2023 before rubber-stamping his side's place at UEFA EURO 2024 with two goals against Slovakia on 13 October 2023.

news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Some moments in pictures
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his intention to retire from international football, bringing an end to his illustrious career with Portugal. The 41-year-old made the announcement in a social media post on Thursday, saying he would “hand back the number 7 shirt” after the November international break. Ronaldo captained Portugal to their first major international trophy at Euro 2016. He also helped the team win the UEFA Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football after glittering Portugal career that spanned 23 years
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football. The 41-year-old Portugal legend has brought an end to his glittering 23-year career for his country after a record-breaking 146 goals in 234 caps. Ronaldo took to social media to confirm the decision on Thursday morning, with the caption "Portugal will always be in me." You can read the statement in full at the bottom of this article.

news.title: Football: Soccer-Ronaldo exits Portugal stage with records intact and farewell clouded by rift
news.lede: Nov 5 (Reuters) - Cristiano Ronaldo has spent more than ⁠two decades making himself impossible to ignore in a Portugal shirt but his farewell announcement on Thursday came through social media rather than a ⁠stadium ovation, with a coaching dispute clouding an extraordinary international career. The 41-year-old has made 234 appearances and scored 146 goals, both men's international ‌records, after a journey that helped turn Portugal from contenders into European champions. Yet the final chapter has become a confrontation over his place in the team. His retirement announcement followed a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, whose decision not to use him against Norway brought the tension between Ronaldo's enduring ambitions and Portugal's changing needs into the open.

news.title: From CR7's infamous World Cup wink to the Jorge Jesus row: 7 controversies that rocked Cristiano Ronaldo'
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo's glittering 23-year international career with Portugal has been defined by extraordinary goalscoring feats, major trophies and a collection of individual records. But alongside the success, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner has also found himself at the centre of several controversies, both on and off the pitch.As the 41-year-old announced his decision to retire from international football after the November 2026 break, his final months in a Portugal shirt were also marked by a public fallout with coach Jorge Jesus.
